name: West Texas Export
description: Stability (voltage/transient) interface limiting power exported from the Permian and West Texas generation pocket to the rest of ERCOT
interface_elements: not public: element lists sit in the GTC Methodology (EMIL NP3-770-M, report 11425), ECEII, digital certificate required
source: ERCOT RPG 29 Jul 2025, 2025 RTP Economic Study: Stability Interface Limits
note: stability-limits deck gives 12,240 MW (2027, Long-Term West Texas Export Study) and 16,200 MW (2030, 2024 RTP); the final 2025 RTP report Table 7 (PDF p.47) gives 12,700 MW for 2027 and 16,200 MW for 2030; the 765-kV import paths lift it from 12.7 to 16.2 GW

name: Panhandle
description: Stability interface limiting wind and solar export out of the Panhandle
interface_elements: not public: element lists sit in the GTC Methodology (EMIL NP3-770-M, report 11425), ECEII, digital certificate required
status: active; 2025 RT rent about $3-9M/month, 9,845 binding SCED intervals in 2025; 2024 RT 12,577 intervals (rank 1)
source: ERCOT RPG 29 Jul 2025, 2025 RTP Economic Study: Stability Interface Limits
last_public_update: 2024-03-01 limits updated after QSA Q1 2024 (notice W-A022124-01)
note: planning limit is the static value used in the 2025 RTP economic study; the RTP appendix P lists Panhandle interface capacity 4,440 MVA

name: Hamilton County
description: Local stability interface in Hamilton County
interface_elements: not public: element lists sit in the GTC Methodology (EMIL NP3-770-M, report 11425), ECEII, digital certificate required
status: active; most frequently binding RT constraint in 2025 (20,326 SCED intervals, rank 1)
source: ERCOT RPG 29 Jul 2025, 2025 RTP Economic Study: Stability Interface Limits
last_public_update: 2024-06-20 limits updated for a local generator model update (ROS GTC update, Jul 2024)
note: limit from the most recent MIS GTC methodology document per the deck

name: McCamey
description: Stability interface in the McCamey area
interface_elements: not public: element lists sit in the GTC Methodology (EMIL NP3-770-M, report 11425), ECEII, digital certificate required
status: active operationally; planning cases need no limit (9,999) because of the Bearkat-North McCamey-Sand Lake 345-kV line (22RPG010, in service 2026)
source: ERCOT RPG 29 Jul 2025, 2025 RTP Economic Study: Stability Interface Limits
last_public_update: 2024-07-03 limits updated for the Cedar Canyon-Noelke-Single Tree-Schneeman Draw-Big Hill second circuit and recent QSA units

name: North to Houston
description: Voltage-stability interface limiting power flowing north into the Houston area
interface_elements: not public: element lists sit in the GTC Methodology (EMIL NP3-770-M, report 11425), ECEII, digital certificate required
status: active; modelled in the 2025 RTP with an hourly profile; 2025 RTP projects it as a top-10 constraint ($26M 2027, $60M 2030 base; $48M/$141M sensitivity)
source: ERCOT RPG 29 Jul 2025, 2025 RTP Economic Study: Stability Interface Limits
note: 5,595 MW is the base rating from a voltage-stability study, scaled by an hourly profile; limits are discounted per the ERCOT Operating Procedure Manual
